Title: How To Use Webhooks

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/how-to-use-webhooks

Markdown Content:
## What Are Webhooks

[Webhook](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#webhook-extension) extensions are user-defined callbacks that are triggered by a real-time notification from Rossum for a related [Queue](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/manage-queues-in-rossum). You can use Webhooks to send notifications to external systems or modify annotation data and display messages to the user. Webhook extensions are similar to [Connectors](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#access-rossum-api) but are more flexible and easier to use.

## How Webhooks Work

To start receiving notifications in your microservice, you have to create a [Hook](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#hook) object of type “webhook.” This Hook object has to be assigned to your [Rossum](https://rossum.ai/intelligent-document-processing/) Queue to receive notifications on various events happening with a document. The Webhook can be [created and assigned to a Queue within the Rossum application](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/rossum-webhook). Once it receives a notification from Rossum, it will forward it to the remote URL of your choice. On this remote URL, you would receive the data, use them to take a certain action, and send a response back to the Hook. One Webhook can be triggered on multiple events, and you can also have more Hooks attached to one Queue.

A Webhook can be notified on one of the following event actions:

*   Annotation status changed,

*   Annotation content was extracted for the first time,

*   User updated the annotation data,

*   Annotation is being moved to the exported state,

*   Email was sent to a Rossum queue.

The Webhooks that are notified on user update events are notified only once as they are interactive. In case the notification wasn’t successful, it is not retried. For the other Webhook events, if the notification call fails with an HTTP status larger than 400, it is retried within 30 seconds for a maximum of 10 attempts. The webhook timeout is 30 seconds, and it is currently global.

## Webhook Requirements

To use a Webhook, you must have your own web server and remote URL ready to listen to the notifications. Suppose you don’t have your own server. In that case, you can use third-party services such as Zapier to build the integration or use some of the [existing Zapier integrations](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/integrate-rossum-with-zapier)].

## Webhooks vs. Connectors

You may be unsure about whether you should choose a [Connector](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#access-rossum-api) or a [Webhook](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#extensions) Extension for your integration. We definitely recommend choosing the Webhook Extension. The Connector Extension is a deprecated extension type present before we implemented Webhooks. But now, Webhooks have multiple advantages over Connectors, namely:

*   There may be multiple Webhooks defined for a single Queue.

*   There is no need to have a hard-coded endpoint name (/validate, /save) in your URL.

*   Webhooks come with a robust retry mechanism in case of the notification failure.

As you can see, a Webhook Extension will provide you with everything that the Connector Extension can and even more.

## When To Use Webhooks

There are many use cases where Webhooks can be very helpful. The most frequent scenarios include situations when you need to:

*   Trigger some actions when an annotation status changes or would like to show the current annotation status to the user in your ERP system.

*   Get the initially extracted data to apply custom rules on them to do initial data validation or supplementary data validation in case of automation.

*   Match user input against the master data in your database (e.g., Vendor matching, Purchase Order matching, or Product matching).

*   Conduct some final validations before data is exported to your ERP to prevent exporting incorrect data.

You can read more detailed steps on how to set up a Webhook [here](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/rossum-webhook). To see a practical example of a Webhook written in Python, check out the following code snippet:

Custom

```
import hashlib
import hmac
from functools import wraps
from typing import Tuple

import flask
from flask_apispec import use_kwargs
import jmespath as jmespath
from flask import jsonify, request
from marshmallow import Schema, fields, EXCLUDE
from werkzeug.exceptions import abort

app = flask.Flask(__name__)
SECRET_KEY = "Your secret key stored in hook.config.secret"  # never store this in code

class UserUpdateSchema(Schema):
   annotation = fields.Dict(required=True, location="json")

   class Meta:
       unknown = EXCLUDE

def hmac_signature_required(f):
   @wraps(f)
   def authorize_request(*args, **kwargs):
       digest = hmac.new(SECRET_KEY.encode(), request.data, hashlib.sha1).hexdigest()
       try:
           prefix, signature = request.headers["X-Elis-Signature"].split("=")
       except ValueError:
           abort(401, "Incorrect header format")
       if not (prefix == "sha1" and hmac.compare_digest(signature, digest)):
           abort(401, "Authorization failed.")
       return f(*args, **kwargs)
   return authorize_request

@app.route("/user_update", methods=["POST"])
@hmac_signature_required
@use_kwargs(UserUpdateSchema())
def api_validate(annotation: dict) -> flask.Response:
   messages, updated_data_fields = zero_string_to_float(annotation["content"])
   return jsonify(
       {
           "messages": messages,
           "operations": updated_data_fields,
       }
   )

def zero_string_to_float(annotation_tree_content: list) -> Tuple[list, list]:
   vat_rate_items = _search_annotation_tree(annotation_tree_content, "item_vat_rate")
   if not vat_rate_items:
       return [{"type": "error", "content": "Column with schema ID 'item_vat_rate' is missing."}], []

   updated_prices: list = []
   for item in vat_rate_items:
       if item["node_value"]:
           if "ZERO" in item["node_value"].upper():
               updated_prices.append({"op": "replace", "id": item["node_id"], "value": {"content": {"value": "0.0"}}})
   return [], updated_prices

def _search_annotation_tree(content: list, schema_id: str):
   return jmespath.search(
       "[].children[].children[].children[?schema_id=='%s'][].{node_id: id, node_value: content.value}"
       % schema_id,
       content,
   )

if __name__ == '__main__':
   app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000)
```

Python

The code above does the following:

*   Provisions an endpoint /user_update where the webhook listens on the notifications sent from Rossum (via @app.route("/user_update", methods=["POST"])

*   Validates received payloads to authorize the request coming from Rossum (in @hmac_signature_required)

*   Serializes the request from Rossum for easier handling (in UserUpdateSchema())

*   Searches the annotation data for the datapoint with id “item_vat_rate” (in _search_ annotation_tree())

*   Changes “ZERO” string to float 0.0

*   Returns the updated data (in api_validate())

Title: Implementing Custom Rules for Automation in Rossum

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/implementing-custom-rules-for-automation-in-rossum

Markdown Content:
Ultimately, to achieve high-quality automation, you should implement custom checks to take advantage of your particular setup. Such cases could be:

*   value extracted from the document can be matched towards expected formats and values (e.g., PO number matching a particular regular expression, or date must be in a certain range)

*   value extracted from the document can be compared to master data (e.g., a list of products)

*   value extracted from the document can be mathematically checked against other values (e.g., amounts, or dates vs. terms)

*   automatically compute and set values for some fields

*   show a message to operators for low confidence score fields

## Hook extension is what you need

Rossum can send the captured data from a document to [a webhook](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/how-to-use-webhooks) or [a serverless function](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/how-to-use-serverless-functions) whenever Rossum's AI Engine is done with the automatic data capture via the Rossum API.

At that moment, the default components of the Rossum platform would already attempt to mark fields as automatically validated (either based on AI confidence scores or some built-in checks). However, this hook can mark more fields as validated based on your custom logic. And crucially, this happens before the Rossum platform determines [whether the document shall be confirmed automatically](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#automation) or left for human review.

When you upload a document to Rossum, it is switched to an "importing" state. Rossum's AI Engine starts processing the document and tries to locate and extract all the necessary fields. Once the automatic extraction is done, the document is switched to the "to_review" state. If you have a hook in place, the data is first sent to the hook when the document switches from the "importing" to "to_review" status.

The extracted data would be sent to your endpoint listening for [action "initialize"](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#webhook-vs-connector). When the hook call returns, Rossum decides whether the document can be automated or whether it will be switched to the "to_review" state by checking the status of individual fields:

*   In the **always** automation level, each field must have a valid value set (non-empty if required).

*   In the **confident** automation level, each field must have at least one [validation source](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#annotation-data).

Custom

```
{
  "request_id": "ae7bc8dd-73bd-489b-a3d2-f5214b209591",
  "timestamp": "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z",
  "hook": "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/hooks/781",
  "action": "user_update",
  "event": "annotation_content",
  "annotation": {
    "document": "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/documents/314621",
    "id": 314521,
    "queue": "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/queues/8236",
    "schema": "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/schemas/223",
    "pages": [
      "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/pages/551518"
    ],
    "modifier": null,
    "modified_at": null,
    "confirmed_at": null,
    "exported_at": null,
    "assigned_at": null,
    "status": "to_review",
    "previous_status": "importing",
    "rir_poll_id": "54f6b91cfb751289e71ddf12",
    "messages": null,
    "url": "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/annotations/314521",
    "content": [
        {
            "id": 1123123,
            "url": "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/annotations/314521/content/1123123",
            "schema_id": "basic_info",
            "category": "section",
            "children": [
              {
                "id": 20456864,
                "url": "https://example.rossum.app/api/v1/annotations/1/content/20456864",
                "content": {
                  "value": "1000.0",
                  "normalized_value": "1000.0",
                  "page": 2},
                 "schema_id": "amount_total"
```

JSON

In the hook, you might implement a functionality that takes the "amount_total" value ("1000.0") and compares it to the summation of the "amount_total_base" + "amount_total_tax" fields.

If the values match, you could fill the "validation_source" which will be taken into account when deciding whether the document can be automated.

The validate endpoint could return the following data as part of the response:

Custom

```
"operations": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "id": "197467",
      "value": {
        "content": {
          "value": "1000.0",
          "position": [916, 168, 1190, 222],
          "rir_position": [916, 168, 1190, 222],
          "rir_confidence": 0.80,
          "page": 1
        },
        "hidden": false,
        "validation_sources": ["connector"]
      }
    }
]
```

JSON

You can see that the response set the "validation_sources" to "connector" which means that the Connector was responsible for validating the correctness of the value.

Additionally, you can show "data_matching" validation source to the users if your extension performed validation of the data against master data database.

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Devs%20-%20Implementing%20Custom%20Rules%20for%20Automation%20in%20Rossum%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A20%3A37Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A37Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=dV350chDKnmobSl7pm9HiF26BOh%2FG8xWgh9EPFipXKw%3D)

_Master data match validation source._

If all fields are automated, the whole document may be automated. But even if this is not achieved, validating fields automatically means less work for the human reviewers, who can use the check marks in the user interface and the ENTER key to focus only on the fields that require manual validation.

> 📘Combining custom rules with other automation components
> 
> 
> Learn [how the different automation components interact together](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/automation-rules-overview) to automate the documents as well as how the automation works with hidden and required fields.

If you would want to change the value from automatic computation on your side or just fill an empty field with a new value, then you can just change the "value" to, say, "1100.0" and empty the "position" of the field since the value is not extracted from the original document anymore.

The validate endpoint could return the following data as part of the response:

Custom

```
"operations": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "id": "197467",
      "value": {
        "content": {
          "value": "1100.0",
          "position": null,
          "rir_position": [916, 168, 1190, 222],
          "rir_confidence": 0.80,
          "page": 1
        },
        "hidden": false,
        "validation_sources": ["connector"]
      }
    }
]
```

JSON

## Showing messages to the operator

The last situation is where you would only like to show the user a message in the UI that they should double-check a specific field. In that case, you can use the "messages" part of the validate hook response. You can choose between "info", "error" and "warning" message types.

Note that each validate call must return the complete list of messages, as this list is not persistent but is overwritten each time the hook is called.

Custom

```
"messages": [
    {
      "content": "Invalid invoice number format",
      "id": "197467",
      "type": "error"
    }
  ]
```

JSON

The ideal opportunity is to combine this with the automation check. If a rule succeeds, the field can be marked as validated. In contrast, if it fails, a warning should be attached to the data point to draw the user's attention to the field.

Title: Import Configuration

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/import-configuration

Markdown Content:
Allows importing Coupa data to your Master Data Hub via the [Coupa Code API](https://compass.coupa.com/en-us/products/product-documentation/integration-technical-documentation/the-coupa-core-api).

## Setup

Create webhook as described in [Integration Setup](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/integration-setup) and use the right link from the table below (according the Rossum environment of configured account)

### Import endpoints

| Environment | Webhook URL |
| --- | --- |
| EU1 Ireland | [https://elis.rossum.ai/svc/scheduled-imports/api/coupa/v1/import](https://elis.rossum.ai/svc/scheduled-imports/api/coupa/v1/import) |
| EU2 Frankfurt | [https://shared-eu2.rossum.app/svc/scheduled-imports/api/coupa/v1/import](https://shared-eu2.rossum.app/svc/scheduled-imports/api/coupa/v1/import) |
| US east coast | [https://us.app.rossum.ai/svc/scheduled-imports/api/coupa/v1/import](https://us.app.rossum.ai/svc/scheduled-imports/api/coupa/v1/import) |
| Japan Tokyo | - |

## Available configuration options

```
{
  "credentials": {
    // Example: "b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184"
    "client_id": "…",
    // Example: "https://mycompany-dev.coupahost.com/"
    "base_api_url": "…",
    // Example: "core.accounting.read"
    "client_scope": "…"
  },
  "import_config": {
    // Query parameters to be passed to the Coupa API.
    "query": {
      // Explicit list of attributes to be imported.
      "fields": []
    },
    // What method to use when inserting data to MDH. Available options: "update", "insert"
    "method": "update",
    // List of attributes that are used to identify a record (used for method "update").
    "id_keys": ["id"],
    // Coupa API endpoint.
    "endpoint": "api/currencies",
    // Name of the dataset in MDH.
    "dataset_name": "COUPA_DEV_currencies_v1",
    // Number of records that will be imported per request.
    "records_per_request": 50
  }
}
```

JSON

### Adding new fields to `query.fields`

In case you want to add a new attribute from the Coupa API to be imported to your Master Data Hub, you need to simply add the attribute as a string to the list. Only keep in mind to replace "-" with "_". For example:

*   Original field name: `attribute-example`

*   New field name: `attribute_example`

If you need to add a new object to the import you need to specify the name of the object and then list all attributes that are nested within the given object. The following example demonstrates import of a nested object which is named `payment-term` and from this object, we need attributes `id` and `name`.

Keep in mind to also replace "-" with "_" in the name of the object:

```
{
  "fields": [
    "id",
    "name",
    "code",
    "allowable_precession",
    "active",
    "updated_at",
    "created_at",
    {
      "payment_term": ["id", "name"]
    }
  ]
}
```

JSON

### Lookup values

See: [Lookup Values API (/lookup_values)](https://compass.coupa.com/en-us/products/product-documentation/integration-technical-documentation/the-coupa-core-api/resources/reference-data-resources/lookup-values-api-(lookup_values))

> 💡 TIP
> 
> 
> Query attributes necessary for differential update are highlighted.

For invoices that are not tied to a purchase order (non-PO-backed), Coupa requires default lookup values to ensure the correct categorization and processing of the invoice. These values help populate essential fields that would otherwise be filled by the purchase order, ensuring the invoice is successfully imported and can proceed through the approval and payment workflows without issues.

```
{
  "credentials": {
    "client_id": "…",
    "base_api_url": "….coupacloud.com/",
    "client_scope": "core.common.read"
  },
  "import_config": {
    "query": {
      "fields": [
        "id",
        "name",
        "external-ref-num",
        "external-ref-code",
        "active",
        {
          "parent": [
            "id",
            "name",
            "active",
            {
              "custom_fields": {}
            },
            {
              "parent": [
                "id",
                "name",
                "active",
                {
                  "custom_fields": {}
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "lookup": ["id", "name", "active"]
        },
        {
          "custom_fields": {}
        }
      ],
      "order_by": "created_at",
      "updated-at[gt_or_eq]": "${last_modified_date}"
    },
    "method": "update",
    "id_keys": ["id"],
    "endpoint": "api/lookup_values",
    "dataset_name": "COUPA_DEV_lookup_values_v1",
    "records_per_request": 50
  }
}
```

Title: Import Documents from File Storage to Rossum

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/import-documents-from-file-storage-to-rossum

Markdown Content:
## What is the Document import from File Storage to Rossum extension

This service enables the automatic import of documents from your file storage, like SFTP or Amazon S3, to a Rossum queue for processing. It regularly connects to your file storage, downloads available files from a specified location, and imports them into a Rossum queue. The following article will guide you through the process of how to set up and utilize this service.

## How to set up the Document import from File Storage to Rossum extension

Setting up the extension takes just a few simple steps.

#### Step 1: Prepare your file storage and the source folder (where documents will be located)

Make sure access permissions and source folder(s) are created.

#### Step 2: Activate your Document Import from File Storage to the Rossum extension

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Import%20Documents%20from%20File%20Storage%20to%20Rossum%20v2%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A45Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A37%3A45Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=iJKmTXm%2Fju3NZGhFtv8mNPPg6ZTKAp%2Fb9Aps5vvL0ao%3D)

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Import%20Documents%20from%20File%20Storage%20to%20Rossum%20v2%2002.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A45Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A37%3A45Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=iJKmTXm%2Fju3NZGhFtv8mNPPg6ZTKAp%2Fb9Aps5vvL0ao%3D)

#### Step 3: Setup the schedule

Define the frequency of your document import job. The schedule definition uses crontab expressions. You can evaluate your expression here.

Here are some examples of commonly used schedules:

*   Once per day: “0 0 * * *”

*   Twice per day (every 12 hours): “0 */12 * * *”

*   Each hour: “0 * * * *”

See [this page](https://crontab.guru/examples.html) for more examples.

#### Step 4: Configure credentials and secrets to your file storage

Credentials and secrets are used to define the type of your file storage – SFTP, Amazon S3 – and to provide the extension with data necessary to access the storage. Different credentials and secrets are needed for different types of file storage – refer to the examples below.

Credentials are defined as part of the hook configuration.

Secrets are defined and safely stored in the extension configuration screen in the Secrets section.

You can add your secrets in the Secrets section edit component. When you click the **Save Changes** button on the configuration screen, your secrets are stored in the function but are not visible anymore for security reasons; instead, the **“__change_me__”** string is shown.

**SFTP Credentials**

```
{
    "credentials": {
        "type": "sftp",
        "host": "",
        "port":,
        "username": ""
    }
}
```

JSON

**SFTP Secrets**

```
{
    "type": "sftp",
    "password": ""
}
```

JSON

**S3 Credentials**

```
{
    "credentials": {
        "type": "s3",
        "bucket_name": ""
    }
}
```

JSON

**S3 Secrets**

```
{
    "type": "s3",
    "access_key_id": "",
    "secret_access_key": ""
}
```

JSON

#### Step 5: Define rules for dataset import

Each rule configures the source folder from where the documents will be imported, what files are valid for importing, and which queue the files will be imported into.

```
{
    "import_rules": [
        {
            "queue_id": 0,
            "path": "",
            "file_match_regex": ""
        }
    ]
}
```

## Configuration example

**Import document into Rossum queue**

The configuration below imports PDF documents from an /inbound folder on your File Storage server and places them into the queue with ID 123. Successfully imported documents are then moved to the folder /archive. Failed imports are moved to **/failed_imports** folder instead.

```
{
    "credentials": { # Credentials are set in a format appropriate for the source system
    },
    "import_rules": [
        {
            "queue_id": 123,
            "path": "/inbound",
            "file_match_regex": ".+\\.pdf",
            "result_actions": {
                "success": {
                    "type": "move",
                    "path": "/archive"
                },
                "failure": {
                    "type": "move",
                    "path": "/failed_imports"
                }
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

JSON

## API Documentation

Please refer to the detailed documentation here: [Document Import](https://elis.task-manager.rossum-ext.app/api/docs#tag/Tasks/operation/file_storage_document_import_api_v1_tasks_file_storage_document_import_post). Under the subsection **settings**, you will find the complete description of available parameters and configuration specifics for different currently supported file storage systems.

Title: Integrate Rossum with Zapier

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/integrate-rossum-with-zapier

Markdown Content:
[Zapier](https://zapier.com/) is a UI-based integration platform, that enables you to connect actions from various applications into simple pipelines called Zaps. Zaps are composed of "Triggers" and "Actions".

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Devs%20-%20Integrate%20Rossum%20with%20Zapier%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A21%3A36Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A32%3A36Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=0HWf6B7kQNmgkL0dQISdulhP5DbswI7m7NVhva7%2F5ic%3D)

Below is an example of a simple Zap, which is triggered when a file is added to a particular folder in your Google Drive. The resulting action is that file being uploaded to a queue in Rossum.

In this guide, we'll go through Triggers and Actions of Rossum app and we will demonstrate their usage by building common use-case Zaps. Before we do that, make sure you have [an account on Zapier](https://zapier.com/sign-up) and that [Zapier supports an application](https://zapier.com/apps) you use. It can be anything from [Xero Accounting Software](https://zapier.com/apps/xero/integrations) to [eBay](https://zapier.com/apps/ebay/integrations).

When setting up an integration, you should first think briefly about what's the best way to actually use Rossum in your workflow - we recommend you batch-review your documents all at once in Rossum, rather than one by one.,

Overview of Rossum Triggers and Actions

In this guide, we'll create a Zap for each of the below. From there you can [build an integration](https://rossum.ai/integrations/) between your favorite application and Rossum.

Upload a Document Action

Zaps can serve to automate [manual document uploads](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/integrate-rossum-with-zapier). This action is pretty straightforward. All you need is a trigger that outputs a file and you can start uploading documents (PDFs and Images) to Rossum. [(Read more about the upload Zap.)](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/managing-documents-in-workspaces-and-queues)

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Devs%20-%20Integrate%20Rossum%20with%20Zapier%2002.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A21%3A36Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A32%3A36Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=0HWf6B7kQNmgkL0dQISdulhP5DbswI7m7NVhva7%2F5ic%3D)

## Document Export Trigger

Once a document is exported in Rossum, this trigger can run a Zap dedicated to propagation of captured data for the individual document back to your system. Captured data can be output either as a file (in a format supported by our [export API](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#relation)) or the data can be exposed in the Zap to allow post-processing. [(Read more about the export Zap.)](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/exporting-document-data-from-rossum-using-zapier)

![Image 3](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Devs%20-%20Integrate%20Rossum%20with%20Zapier%2003.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A21%3A36Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A32%3A36Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=0HWf6B7kQNmgkL0dQISdulhP5DbswI7m7NVhva7%2F5ic%3D)

## Export Confirmed Documents Action

It is often easier to export data from many documents at once. If you have confirmed state enabled on your queue, you can use this action to trigger batch export of all documents pending in "Confirmed" tab. Zap with this action is designed to be paired with a Zap with **Document Export Trigger**. [(Read more about the batch export Zap.)](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/batch-export-of-documents-from-rossum-using-zapier)

![Image 4](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Devs%20-%20Integrate%20Rossum%20with%20Zapier%2004.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A21%3A36Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A32%3A36Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=0HWf6B7kQNmgkL0dQISdulhP5DbswI7m7NVhva7%2F5ic%3D)

Title: Integration Configuration

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/integration-configuration

Markdown Content:
To configure an access token in NetSuite for SOAP communication, especially when there is no integration user yet, involves several steps that include creating an integration record in NetSuite, setting up a role with the necessary permissions, creating an integration user, and then generating the access token. Below is a step-by-step guide:

## 1. Create an Integration Record in NetSuite

1.   **Log in to your NetSuite account** as an administrator ([https://system.netsuite.com/](https://system.netsuite.com/)).

2.   Navigate to **Setup → Integrations → Manage Integrations → New**.

3.   Fill in the **Name** of the integration and ensure that **State** is enabled.

4.   Check the **Token-Based Authentication** to use token-based auth along with SOAP.

5.   **Save** the integration. Note the **Consumer Key** and **Consumer Secret** presented upon saving; these are important for authentication.

> ⚠️ WARNING ⚠️
> 
> 
> Remember to save the **Consumer Key**and **Consumer Secret** for later.

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/NetSuite%20Integration%20configuration%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A13%3A11Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A25%3A11Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=MiVwxWpcxDbMvHg9Ods8CxN8EZxzilxNmPlOVMaT9C8%3D)

## 2. Create a Role with necessary permissions

1.   Navigate to **Setup → Users/Roles → Manage Roles → New**.

2.   Provide a **Name** for the role and assign it permissions necessary for the operations the integration will perform. At a minimum, for SOAP communication, you might need permissions like **SOAP Web Services**, **Log in using Access Tokens**, and any specific permissions related to the data you wish to access or modify (Lists).

3.   **Save** the role.

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/NetSuite%20Integration%20configuration%2002.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A13%3A11Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A25%3A11Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=MiVwxWpcxDbMvHg9Ods8CxN8EZxzilxNmPlOVMaT9C8%3D)

## 3. Create an Integration User

1.   Go to **Lists → Employees → Employees → New**.

2.   Fill in the necessary information for the user. Under the **Access** tab, ensure you **Check** the **Give Access** option, set a **Password**, and **Assign the Role** you created earlier.

3.   **Save** the employee record.

> 💡 TIP
> 
> 
> While it is technically possible to reuse already existing employee account, we recommend creating a new one for the integration. This way, the integration won't get broken when the employee account gets deactivated.

## 4. Generate the Access Token

1.   Navigate to **Setup → Users/Roles → Access Tokens → New**.

2.   Select the **Application Name** (the integration you created in Step 1), the **User**, and the **Role** you've assigned to this integration.

3.   **Save** to generate the Token ID and Token Secret.

> ⚠️ WARNING ⚠️
> 
> 
> Remember to save the **Token ID** and **Token Secret** for later.

## 5. Use the Access Token in SOAP communication

With the Consumer Key, Consumer Secret, Token ID, and Token Secret, you can now configure Rossum.ai SOAP client for communication with NetSuite:

Secrets:

```
{
  "consumer_key": "…", // change
  "consumer_secret": "…", // change
  "token_key": "…", // change
  "token_secret": "…", // change
  "rossum_username": "system.user@rossum.example", // change
  "rossum_password": "…" // change
}
```

JSON

Import/Export configuration:

```
{
  "netsuite_settings": {
    "account": "XXX_SB1", // Case sensitive!
    "concurrency_limit": 4,
    "wsdl_url": "https://XXX-sb1.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/wsdl/v2024_1_0/netsuite.wsdl",
    "service_url": "https://XXX-sb1.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/NetSuitePort_2024_1",
    "service_binding_name": "{urn:platform_2024_1.webservices.netsuite.com}NetSuiteBinding"
  }
}
```

JSON

Account ID (`account`) can be found under **Setup → Company → Company Information**.

## Important notes

*   Ensure your NetSuite account has the **Token-Based Authentication** feature enabled. This can be checked and enabled under **Setup → Company → Enable Features → SuiteCloud**.

*   The permissions assigned to the role will dictate what operations can be performed through the SOAP API. Make sure to adjust these according to the least privilege principle, granting only the permissions necessary for the tasks the integration will perform.

This process sets up a secure method for your application or integration to communicate with NetSuite using SOAP. If you encounter any specific issues during setup or need more detailed instructions, NetSuite's official documentation and support resources can provide additional guidance tailored to the latest platform updates and best practices.

Markdown Content:
The following article guides you through the Coupa integration setup. It consists of two mandatory parts: Coupa configuration and Rossum hook configuration.

## Configuring Coupa

The main prerequisite is to have a valid Coupa user with needed permissions (see OAuth 2.0 scopes). If you don't have a user with needed permission, ask your admin to create it.

> 💡 TIP
> 
> 
> You can always (also) check the official documentation [OAuth 2.0 Getting Started with Coupa API](https://compass.coupa.com/en-us/products/total-spend-management-platform/integration-playbooks-and-resources/integration-knowledge-articles/oauth-2.0-getting-started-with-coupa-api)

1.   Login to the Coupa web admin at URL `https://[example-company].coupacloud.com`

2.   Go to the Setup, search for keyword `oauth` and click the one result **OAuth2/OpenID Connect Clients**

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Coupa%20Integration%20setup%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A13%3A56Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A25%3A56Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=U7DF8wb5uNP4W3uI7Yi9dF%2FErbslko%2Fm4n7lBcJyqVk%3D)

1.   Create a new Client and make sure that you have selected a Grant type with `Client Credentials` option and save it.

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Coupa%20Integration%20setup%2002.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A13%3A56Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A25%3A56Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=U7DF8wb5uNP4W3uI7Yi9dF%2FErbslko%2Fm4n7lBcJyqVk%3D)

1.   Find the user prepared for the integration and note the values `Identifier` and `Secrets`. You will need it for every hook setup later

![Image 3](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Coupa%20Integration%20setup%2003.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A13%3A56Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A25%3A56Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=U7DF8wb5uNP4W3uI7Yi9dF%2FErbslko%2Fm4n7lBcJyqVk%3D)

1.   For start, these scopes should work for basic integration `core.accounting.read, core.common.read, core.invoice.create, core.invoice.read, core.invoice.write, core.purchase_order.read, core.supplier.read` - you can copy and paste it exactly like this when using the Postman collection provided by Coupa

## Configuring Rossum

Coupa service (integration) is provided by Rossum.ai in the form of webhook. To start using Coupa (either imports or exports), follow these steps:

### Webhook in UI

1.   Login to your Rossum account.

2.   Navigate to **Extensions** → **My extensions**.

3.   Click on **Create extension**.

4.   Set the following fields:

    1.   Name: `Coupa: Import/Export [what]`

    2.   Trigger events: `Manual` (later also `Scheduled`)

    3.   Extension type: `Webhook`

    4.   URL (see [Import configuration](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/import-configuration) and [Export configuration](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/export-configuration))

    5.   Token owner of the extension (typically a system user)

5.   Click **Create the webhook**.

6.   Fill `Configuration` (see [Import configuration examples](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/import-configuration) or [Export configuration examples](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/export-configuration))

7.   Fill `Secrets` fields.

### Setting hook secrets schema (optional):

Optional step is it cannot be done via UI (but can be done either via API or via [prd deployment tool](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/sandboxes))

```
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "client_secret": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "API OAuth Client secret"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

JSON

As a result of this change, it is easier to update the hook secrets (and to know what is in the secrets). You will see the following value in the hook secrets that can be easily modified:

```
{
  "client_secret": "__change_me__"
}
```

JSON

## Initial test

You can invoke the webhook manually using **curl** (for example):

```
curl --location --request POST 'https://[company-example].rossum.app/api/v1/hooks/[hook-id]/invoke' \
--header 'Authorization: token [token]' \
--data ''
```

Bash

Then go to the Rossum Extension Logs and observe the content

## Available configuration options

Title: Interactive Bounding Boxes in Rossum

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/interactive-bounding-boxes-in-rossum

Markdown Content:
## What are interactive bounding boxes

During the process of validating data extracted from documents, you may have noticed that the values on the document are surrounded by blue borders. These borders, also known as bounding boxes, serve the purpose of selecting values on the document. To enhance the annotation process and make it more intuitive, we are introducing a new and improved version of bounding boxes.

## Changes on the validation screen

### Interactive bounding boxes

*   Hovering over an bounding box enables you to check which field holds the corresponding value.

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Interactive%20Bounding%20Boxes%20in%20Rossum%2001v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A28%3A24Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A39%3A24Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=07o9%2BEbxMB6quI27CcU50bsJXeTK3hmzeydTZha7OCQ%3D)

*   Clicking on an extracted value redirects you to the associated field.

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Interactive%20Bounding%20Boxes%20in%20Rossum%2002v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A28%3A24Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A39%3A24Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=07o9%2BEbxMB6quI27CcU50bsJXeTK3hmzeydTZha7OCQ%3D)

*   When a field is selected, clicking on another extracted value on the document redirects you to the field linked to that value, rather than changing the value in the selected field.

![Image 3](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Interactive%20Bounding%20Boxes%20in%20Rossum%2003v2.gif?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A28%3A24Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A39%3A24Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=07o9%2BEbxMB6quI27CcU50bsJXeTK3hmzeydTZha7OCQ%3D)

*   Adjusting the size of a bounding box is now easier, as you can modify it using the corners.

![Image 4](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Interactive%20Bounding%20Boxes%20in%20Rossum%2004v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A28%3A24Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A39%3A24Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=07o9%2BEbxMB6quI27CcU50bsJXeTK3hmzeydTZha7OCQ%3D)

*   These enhancements significantly simplify and expedite the annotation process.

### Highlighted values with different colours

*   **Yellow**: Initial extracted values before user review.

*   **Green**: Values manually checked by a user.

*   **Red**: Values that prevent document confirmation, such as incorrectly formatted extracted data.

![Image 5](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Interactive%20Bounding%20Boxes%20in%20Rossum%2005v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A28%3A24Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A39%3A24Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=07o9%2BEbxMB6quI27CcU50bsJXeTK3hmzeydTZha7OCQ%3D)

![Image 6](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Interactive%20Bounding%20Boxes%20in%20Rossum%2006v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A28%3A24Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A39%3A24Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=07o9%2BEbxMB6quI27CcU50bsJXeTK3hmzeydTZha7OCQ%3D)

This change provides valuable insights into the predicted data. You can promptly identify values that hinder document processing or fields that require additional annotations to improve AI confidence.

### Suggested bounding boxes

If you wish to review other recognised values on the document available for annotation, you can easily display suggested bounding boxes. Simply hold down the **ALT** (**OPTION** on MAC) key on your keyboard. Please keep in mind that it has to be constantly pressed to display the suggestions.

By incorporating these improvements, the annotation process becomes more user-friendly and efficient than ever before.

![Image 7](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Interactive%20Bounding%20Boxes%20in%20Rossum%2007v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A28%3A24Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A39%3A24Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=07o9%2BEbxMB6quI27CcU50bsJXeTK3hmzeydTZha7OCQ%3D)

# Introducing Formula Fields: A New Way to Transform Your Data

*    Published on Feb 24, 2025 

*    1 minute(s) read 

Article summary

[Prev](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/rejecting-documents-in-rossum "Rejecting Documents in Rossum")[Next](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/formula-fields-in-rossum "Formula Fields in Rossum")
We’re excited to introduce Formula Fields, a powerful new feature that simplifies data transformation within Rossum. With Formula Fields, you can create custom formulas to set field values, perform calculations, normalize data, and more—all without writing a single line of code, thanks to Copilot!

![Image 3: Introducing Formula Fields- A New Way to Transform Your Data 01](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Introducing%20Formula%20Fields-%20A%20New%20Way%20to%20Transform%20Your%20Data%2001.gif?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A39Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A40%3A39Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=bOxlIXvCeZZECCWRT2tHSDVKul1QeDpW%2BVI0MZvkCJ4%3D)

## Benefits of Formula Fields

**No-code simplicity**: Create custom transformations tailored to your specific needs, without having to write a single line of code.

**Easy maintenance and clarity**: Transformations are defined directly in the relevant field, making them simple to understand and maintain.

**Performance**: Formula Fields are super fast, fitting even the most complex use cases.

**Automatic execution order**: Formula Fields run your workflows in the correct sequence automatically—no manual intervention needed.

**Streamlined workflows**: Say goodbye to multiple extensions. Formula Fields do the work in one step, reducing complexity.

Formula Fields are now also optionally editable, allowing users to overwrite calculated values in special cases when needed.

## Deprecation of legacy extensions

To align with this new functionality, we will be deprecating the following legacy extensions from the Rossum Store:

*   Copy & Paste Values

*   Find & Replace Values

*   Value Mapping

*   Date Calculations

*   Numeric Calculations

## What does this mean for you?

The legacy extensions will first be deprecated in the Rossum Store, with full removal scheduled for October 28th, as they are fully covered by Formula Fields. Existing setups won’t be affected.

While new instances won’t be available after that date, current configurations will remain unchanged as our support and technical teams explore migration options in your setups, which will be consulted with you well ahead.

## Where may I try Formula Fields?

Head over to your queue settings and start experimenting—try creating a Formula Field yourself using Copilot, and see how easy it is to streamline your workflows.

[Find out more about Formula Fields](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/formula-fields-in-rossum).

Markdown Content:
When reviewing documents in Rossum, there are multiple ways of moving between Data Fields, confirming them, and editing them. Over time, operators find the most suitable way for them to review documents.

Here are some tips on how to speed up the reviewing process using various keyboard shortcuts when working with header fields, tables or search panel:

## Keyboard shortcuts list

TAB Move to the next field in the sequence.
ENTER Move between fields that don’t have the checkmark displayed next to them and await your review.
CTRL + Shift ⇧ + A (Windows)

CMD ⌘ + Shift ⇧ + A (Mac)Add a new value to the end of the multivalue header field.
Shift ⇧ + Click Add a new value to the multivalue header field without pressing the “Add a value” button.

You can hold SHIFT and keep clicking on various values to add them to the multivalue field.

If you hold down SHIFT and click on one of the values already added to a multivalue field (on the left panel of validation screen), it will highlight all the values above, including the one you clicked on, and allow you to delete them.
Hold ALT (Windows)

Hold OPTION ⌥ (MAC)Displays suggested bounding boxes – values recognised on document and available for annotation.

#### Tables

TAB Move between fields in the direction from the beginning of a row to its end.
UP ↑, DOWN ↓, LEFT ←, RIGHT →You can use the arrows to move around the table space.
CTRL + Shift ⇧ + A (Windows)

CMD ⌘ + Shift ⇧ + A (Mac)Add a new row to the end of a table.
Drag & Drop You can click on a cell and drag its bottom right corner to the cells below it to copy its values.
Hold ALT (Windows)

Hold OPTION ⌥ (MAC)Displays suggested bounding boxes – values recognised on document and available for annotation.

#### Search Panel

CTRL + Shift ⇧ + F (Windows)

CMD ⌘ + Shift ⇧ + F (Mac)Use this shortcut to open or close Search Panel.
Escape Closes Search Panel.
ENTER While in Search Panel, use it to navigate to the next searched value.
Shift ⇧ + ENTER While in Search Panel, use it to navigate to the previous searched value.

Title: Labels in Rossum: Streamline Document Organisation and Workload Distribution

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/labels-in-rossum

Markdown Content:
## What are the labels in Rossum

Labels are designed to enhance your document organisation capabilities. Now you can tag annotations with customised labels of your choice. The tool allows you to efficiently manage your documents, distribute work among annotators, and quickly locate relevant information in your queues.

## Activating the feature on your account

Labels are available in the Enterprise and Ultimate Rossum plans. If you are unsure whether this feature is included in your plan, please contact your account manager or support team [support@rossum.ai](mailto:support@rossum.ai).

## How to create and manage labels

The ability to create and manage labels within your account is limited to users with an Admin role.

To add a new label or remove an existing one, navigate to the "Settings" section in your account. You can either tap or hover to reveal the Settings sections.

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2002.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

All labels associated with your account can be found in the "Labels" tab.

If you need to modify an existing label, simply click on the pencil icon, and a pop-up window will appear with further options. Same thing if you want to remove an existing label, just click on the bin icon. Please be aware that deleting a label will result in its permanent removal from the organisation, and from all the annotations connected to it.

![Image 3](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2003.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

To create a new label, click on the button on the upper right corner and a pop-up window will appear.

![Image 4](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2004.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

You can conveniently create new labels or access the settings directly from the the queue view. Additional choices become accessible when assigning labels to annotations.

![Image 5](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2005.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

Labels can also be also managed through the [API](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#label).

## Working with labels

Upon activation, you will notice a new column titled "Labels" in your queue view. To assign labels to specific annotations, you can select the relevant annotations and choose the appropriate tags from the provided options. It is possible to assign multiple labels to a single annotation.

![Image 6](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2006.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

![Image 7](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2007.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

Utilising the power of this feature, you can easily filter and search for specific records within your queues, enabling you to find relevant information swiftly. It is important to note that if you switch to another queue, the applied filters will remain active, ensuring a seamless and uninterrupted workflow.

![Image 8](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Labels%20in%20Rossum%2008.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A24%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A35%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=Ud5aYnoVCslnNz%2FcAVQKd2WRTmctUh8tcI%2FTYS6U4bU%3D)

## Limitations of the feature

While labels in Rossum offer valuable benefits, the feature has a limitation:

*   You have to assign labels manually as there is no automatic labelling functionality integrated at this time.

Title: Languages Supported by Rossum

Markdown Content:
Rossum lets you process documents in many different languages. Here’s a complete list of the supported languages and the features available for each one.

## Legacy Data Capture

Before Aurora, Rossum could recognize the following languages: Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Hungarian, Italian, Lithuanian, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Brazilian Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Catalan, and Swedish. We also provided support for Japanese and Chinese.

With the release of Aurora 1.5, the list of supported languages expanded significantly. We now offer full or partial support for 276 languages. This article provides all the details.

## Rossum Aurora – Fully Supported Languages

For all the languages listed below, **Document Language Classification** is available, meaning Rossum will automatically recognize the language (the document language can be predicted). **Instant Learning** is also supported, which means our AI can learn from annotations in these languages.

Most of these languages support **pre-trained fields**, meaning the AI can provide predictions for certain fields right away, without needing extra training or previous annotations. You can find the [full list of fields here](https://rossum.app/api/docs/#extracted-field-types).

For some languages, we support full or partial recognition of **handwritten text**. Partial handwriting recognition means that some diacritics may not be recognised.

❌ – Not available

Article summary

[Prev](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/alternative-python-solution "Alternative Python Solution")[Next](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/configuration-examples-4 "Configuration Examples")
**Line items grouping** extension allows for grouping line items based on given SQL criteria. This is handy when the downstream system has some restrictions such as only one unique line item per invoice.

## Installation

Line items grouping service is provided by Rossum.ai in the form of webhook. To start using the extension, follow these steps:

1.   Login to your Rossum account.

2.   Navigate to **Extensions** → **My extensions**.

3.   Click on **Create extension**.

4.   Fill the following fields:

    1.   Name: `Line items grouping`

    2.   Trigger events: `Document content: Initialize, Started, Updated`

    3.   Queues where the extension should be executed

    4.   Extension type: `Webhook`

    5.   URL (see [Available endpoints](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/line-items-grouping#available-endpoints) below)

5.   Click **Create the webhook**.

6.   Fill `Configuration` field (visit [Configuration examples](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/configuration-examples-4) page).

Title: Manage Queues in Rossum

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/manage-queues-in-rossum

Markdown Content:
What exactly is a queue in Rossum, and how can you manage queues and documents?

A queue is Rossum’s basic unit that helps you organize documents and manage workflow. You should create a separate Queue for every document type (such as invoices, packing lists, claims, etc.). Within a queue, you can configure custom automation settings. You can also add extensions to improve document workflows when linking up with other systems.

## How to create a queue

After your first login, you will be prompted to choose the document type you want to process to create a new queue. To do so, simply select the document category you wish to have in that queue:

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

However, as you can see, other options are available after custom training. If you need some of those, click on it and request a demo. Our AI experts will show you how Rossum can automate your document processing for the selected document type.

Then, you need to name the queue, specify the workspace, and indicate the origin of the documents. This information is necessary to set the correct rules for the documents.

When you choose one of the regions, Rossum will automatically create your first queue. Now you can import/send documents to it.

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2002.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

If you want to create another queue, follow the steps below:

1.   Click on the “+” sign at the top of the left panel or three-dotted drop-down menu next to the workspace name.

2.   Click the “Add new queue” button.

3.   Select the document type.

4.   Place the queue name, select the Workspace and the documents’ region and click on “Add queue”.

![Image 3](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2003.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

![Image 4](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2004.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

## How to rename a queue

1.   Click on the three-dotted drop-down menu visible next to the queue’s name.

2.   Select the ‘Rename’ option.

![Image 5](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2005.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

## How to move a queue

If you need to move the queue to a new workspace, you can do so by:

1.   Click on the three-dotted drop-down menu visible next to the queue’s name.

2.   Select the ‘Move’ option.

3.   Then select a workspace you wish to move the queue.

![Image 6](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2006.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

## How to duplicate a queue

If you need to duplicate the queue to a new workspace, you can do so by:

1.   Click on the three-dotted drop-down menu visible next to the queue’s name.

2.   Select the ‘duplicate’ option.

3.   Then choose what other settings you want to duplicate to the new queue.

> If you want to duplicate a queue assigned to a dedicated engine, please reach out to your Account Manager or support@rossum.ai.

![Image 7](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2007.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

## How to delete a queue

1.   Click on the three-dotted drop-down menu visible next to the queue’s name.

2.   Select the ‘Delete’ option.

![Image 8](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2008.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

> You can delete a queue even if it contains documents.
> 
> 
> When you delete a queue, a warning will appear, asking you to confirm your choice. To proceed, you must check all confirmation options.

![Image 9](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Queues%2009.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A30%3A01Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A42%3A01Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=qifmAXjtYmYDeFUs9TeoZRFVMTphjVMnd20KUeFpHeY%3D)

## What is a Workplace?

A Workspace is a top-level container for related queues. It’s a good idea to create separate workspaces for different departments, business units, or clients – to group queues in a logical way.

## How to create a new Workspace

1.   Click the “**+**” sign next to “**All documents**” in the top left corner of the app.

2.   Select the “**Add workspace**” option.

3.   Enter a descriptive name for the workspace and confirm. The new workspace will appear in your left panel.

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2001.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2002.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

> Note: The newly created workspace does not include any Queues. You need to create a new Queue and assign it to the workspace.

## How to rename a Workspace

1.   Click on the three dots next to the workspace’s name (if you see a number instead, hover over it to reveal the tree dots).

2.   Select the ‘**Rename**’ option.

![Image 3](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Manage%20Workspaces%20in%20Rossum%20new%2011.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

## How to add a Queue to a Workspace

There are two ways of doing this:

1.   Click on the “**+**” next to “**All documents**” in the top left corner or three-dotted drop-down menu next to the workspace name (if you see a number instead, hover over it to reveal the tree dots).

2.   Select the ‘**Add queue**’ option

![Image 4](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2003.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

![Image 5](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2004.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

1.   A new window will appear. Select the document type that your new queue will use:

![Image 6](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2005.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

1.   Place your new queue’s name, select the Workspace where you want to place it and click “**Add queue**”.

![Image 7](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2006.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

## How to delete a Workspace

If you no longer need a workspace, you can delete it. To do so:

1.   Click on the three dots next to the workspace’s name (if you see a number instead, hover over it to reveal the tree dots).

2.   Select the ‘**Delete**’ option.

3.   Click on the red “**Permanently delete workspace**” button.

![Image 8](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2007.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

![Image 9](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2008.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

> All queues must first be removed before a workspace can be deleted.

![Image 10](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Article%20-%20Manage%20Workspaces%2009.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A18%3A31Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A29%3A31Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=r16TCim9VseLBztk%2BOae0pgdKAT7xPFBgVFPcqYF0Q0%3D)

Title: Managing Documents in Workspaces and Queues

URL Source: https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/managing-documents-in-workspaces-and-queues

Markdown Content:
*    Updated on Aug 5, 2025 
*    Published on Feb 24, 2025 

*    4 minute(s) read 

[Prev](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/how-to-manage-users "Manage Users in Rossum")[Next](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/docs/all-documents-dashboard-in-rossum "All Documents Dashboard in Rossum")
## What is the difference between a workspace and a queue?

This article will show how to manage workspaces and queues and move documents in Rossum. But first, let’s go over the basics.

[Workspaces](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/manage-workspaces-in-rossum) allow you to group related queues into one organizational unit. Think of the workspace as a large organizational unit representing a specific customer (if you are a business process outsourcing company) or department. You could then use [Queues](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/manage-queues-in-rossum) to separate documents by document type. However, your workspace and queue hierarchy design depends heavily on your use case.

## How to import your first documents to Rossum

First, let’s review how to upload documents to a specific queue. You have several options from which you can choose.

### Manual upload via the web application

Manual upload is the best option for getting started quickly. Click the **Upload files** button in the app and select the files you want to upload. This method is more suitable for a small number of documents. If you need to upload more than 100 documents in one go, use one of the other methods listed below.

![Image 1](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2001v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

### Import via email

Rossum can ingest PDF and image attachments from emails as documents. This import option is a popular method for companies that handle their supplier traffic directly in Rossum. Each queue has a unique email address so you can forward documents to the email address specified on the upload screen or in the queue’s settings.

![Image 2](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2002v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

![Image 3](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2003v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

Rossum will select attachments that it can process as documents. It will try to filter out image attachments that are just banners or are unrelated. It is important to note that Rossum does not process the body of the email itself – HTML documents are not processed.

### Automatic import

If the source system is also in the cloud, you can use [Zapier](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/integrate-rossum-with-zapier) to automate the import process when the email is insufficient (for example, binding the import to a shared drive upload). We’ve already prepared a [sample upload Zap](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/upload-a-document-to-rossum-using-zapier). An RPA workflow is the most convenient option if you must access the source system via a local desktop.

### API import

The ultimate method for importing documents is using the upload API. The API documentation has a detailed reference and a [quick start guide to upload your first document using the API](https://elis.rossum.ai/api/docs/#quick-api-tutorial). You can also check our code examples showing how to automatically upload documents in [Python](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/python-for-uploading-data-in-rossum-api), [JavaScript](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/javascript-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api), [Java](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/java-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api), [BASH](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/shell-script-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api), [R-language](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/r-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api), [Go](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/go-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api-1), [Rust](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/rust-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api), [Ruby](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/ruby-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api), and [C#](https://developers.rossum.ai/docs/c-for-uploading-documents-in-rossum-api).

Once you upload the document, it will end up in a particular workspace and queue.

## How to move the documents between the queues

Once the documents are in Rossum, you may need to move one of them to another queue because:

*   you accidentally uploaded a document to the wrong queue.

*   you receive all documents in one queue and then assign them to the appropriate queues

*   you have a separate queue where other users approve validated documents.

To move one or more documents to another queue, you first must select them and the click the **Move** icon in the popup menu and choose where to move the document(s).

![Image 4](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2004v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

![Image 5](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2005v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

If you want to move only one document, you can also use the **Move** button under the three dots shown in the image below. This option is available in all tabs in Rossum (To review, Postponed, Confirmed, Exported, Rejected, and Deleted) and in the simplified view.

![Image 6](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2006v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

You can also move a document between queues while annotating it. Use the three dots shown in the image below to do this.

![Image 7](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2006-5v2.png.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

## How to move the documents between the tabs

In addition to moving documents between queues, you may also need to move documents between different tabs within the same queue. Rossum usually does this automatically as you process the documents (You can read more about the lifecycle of a document in Rossum in [this article](https://knowledge-base.rossum.ai/help/docs/guide-to-the-document-lifecycle)).

However, you may have accidentally deleted a document or wish to re-edit a document that has already been exported. In these cases:

1.   Select the document and click the **Move** icon.

2.   Choose the same queue where the document is currently located.

3.   Confirm the action by clicking the **Move** button.

Doing this will cause the document to be moved to this queue’s **To Review** tab.

## How to delete a document

Sometimes you may need to delete documents. You have a few ways to do it in the Rossum app.

If you want to delete a single document:

1.   Hover over the document you want to delete.

2.   Once you highlight it, click on the three-dotted menu.

3.   Select the **Delete** option.

Another way to delete documents is to select one or multiple documents using the checkbox icon. After you choose all the documents you want to remove, click the **Delete** icon on the pop-up menu.

![Image 8](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2007v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

Once you click the Delete icon, Rossum will ask you to confirm your decision and delete the document.

![Image 9](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2008v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

When you delete a document, its status becomes deleted.

In a simplified view (without tabs), you will see it with the tag “Deleted” on your document list.

![Image 10](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2009v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

If you use the interface with tabs, the document will be visible in the Deleted tab.

![Image 11](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2010v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

You can restore a deleted document and change its status to to_review in order to process it again. To do so:

1.   select the document,

2.   click the Move icon in the pop-up menu,

3.   choose the queue,

4.   click the Move button.

## How to purge a document

You may occasionally need to remove documents from Rossum permanently. Purging is a feature that will allow you to do so.

Please remember that the documents you wish to purge must first have deleted status.

To purge document(s):

1.   Select the document(s) you want to purge (either in the Deleted tab or in the main queue window in the simplified view).

2.   In the pop-up menu, click the Purge icon.

![Image 12](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2011v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)

1.   Confirm your decision to purge selected document(s).

![Image 13](https://cdn.document360.io/1bb6f6bc-c04c-4ace-a1e8-8c4cfd3fbc98/Images/Documentation/Managing%20Documents%20in%20Workspaces%20And%20Queues%2012v2.png?sv=2022-11-02&spr=https&st=2026-05-22T07%3A19%3A26Z&se=2026-05-22T07%3A33%3A26Z&sr=c&sp=r&sig=pF%2F8X%2BFiVQf7ussQp9abLYV4%2BfziyfiKkpbiSf8AtgY%3D)
